name: 01-title
title: Trick or Trace
notes: Opening or holding graphic. Establish the outcome: detect, investigate, report. The wizard is a seasonal treatment of the original frog, not a new product logo.

name: 02-architecture
title: Overall architecture
notes: Read the top row left to right, then follow the event into Runtime. Intake Lambda only dispatches. Bidirectional tool connectors carry requests and results. Bedrock provides the model; S3 stores incident snapshots; AgentCore Memory stores lessons. Report text and mention are posted directly to Slack by application code. The current demo does not post a ticket or report URL. Not every deployed support resource is drawn.

name: 03-strands-loop
title: The Strands agent loop
notes: The model chooses a tool; Strands executes it and feeds back the result. The loop can continue through several tools or finish with an answer. This is a conceptual loop, not a separate deployment architecture. Reasoning does not require displaying private model reasoning.

name: 03b-what-is-a-harness
title: Agent = Model + Harness
notes: Bridge from the agent loop to the configured Strands product. Say: “The model chooses a tool call, but software has to execute it, return the result, and make the next model call. That software is the harness. It also manages the information and state the model needs as work continues. Strands harness assembles those pieces with defaults we can customize.” Agent = Model + Harness is a useful system-design framing, explicitly used by LangChain, rather than a formal universal definition. The six boxes group common harness responsibilities; they are not a claim that every harness ships every feature. Hooks are extension points where developers can implement logging, checks or approvals; their presence alone is not an enforced security boundary or an automatic approval workflow. The next graphic describes this demo’s installed Strands defaults. Research: LangChain, The Anatomy of an Agent Harness (2026-03-10); Anthropic, Effective harnesses for long-running agents (2025-11-26); current Strands harness documentation. See SOURCES.md.

name: 04-harness-defaults
title: What harness gives you
notes: Use while the basic TypeScript example is visible. Defaults verified against harness 0.3.1 and SDK 1.22.0. Local file tools and shell are not automatically isolated. Sessions default to .agent/sessions; file memory defaults to .agent/memory; .agent/skills is discovered if present. Short demos may not exercise compaction or produce useful memories. Default web search is provider-dependent, so it is not represented as universally enabled.

name: 05-runtime-memory
title: harness on Runtime with sessions and memory
notes: Runtime hosts the process; it is not the durable memory store. Our current TypeScript integration uses SessionManager and S3Storage for snapshots, and AgentCoreMemoryStore for lessons. This is a demo integration choice, not a claim that AgentCore lacks short-term memory. Extraction is asynchronous. A confirmed engineer outcome is stronger evidence for a future lesson than the agent’s initial hypothesis.

name: 06-runtime-interpreter
title: Runtime and AWS MCP execution
notes: The model generates Python tool arguments. Strands sends them over signed Streamable HTTP to the managed AWS MCP endpoint. AWS MCP executes the script remotely and returns evidence or an error. The application assumes the scoped investigation role to sign requests. No local STDIO server or host shell executes these investigation scripts. The underlying managed sandbox compute technology is not asserted here. This replaces the former interpreter diagram; its existing filename is retained for presenter bookmarks.

name: 07-mcp-iam
title: AWS MCP and the investigation role
notes: Read the numbered chain carefully: application code uses the Runtime role to assume the investigation role through STS; support/aws.ts signs AWS MCP requests with the temporary credentials. Managed AWS MCP executes the requested AWS operations under the investigation identity. IAM bounds those operations. AWS MCP executes remotely; do not draw it as running in the agent container. Some CloudWatch metrics and Logs Insights result permissions require Resource:* and have a broader read scope than the named sample resources. IAM does not make untrusted logs safe instructions or block every possible data-exfiltration route.

name: 08-skills-context-memory
title: What gives the agent context?
notes: Skills contain reusable instructions and procedures. Session storage persists messages, tool results, and agent state so a session can be restored. Long-term memory retains facts and lessons across sessions. The downward arrows show possible context sources, not a claim that each investigation reads all three. During one invocation, the agent loop retains its working conversation and tool results; it does not need to restore a saved session to use an earlier result. This demo starts a fresh incident session and does not demonstrate a follow-up that restores its snapshot. S3 preserves those snapshots outside the runtime for later inspection or restoration. Local storage could simplify a disposable demo, but files in the current runtime configuration are ephemeral. The shared storage backend can also hold offloaded context; that is distinct from restoring a session snapshot. See SOURCES.md for storage and session documentation.
